title: Write and save a note
prerequisites: Notepad is open. Your other tabs stay as they are.
concept: Notepad keeps plain text, like a list or a quick note. Saving puts it in a file you can open again later.
recap: You wrote a note and saved it: a new tab, your text, File, Save as, then Save.

check.question: Quick check: which menu has Save as?
check.explain: The File menu holds everything about the file itself: new, open, save and print.

speech.demonstrate: Click the plus next to your tabs. It opens a fresh, empty page.
speech.guide: Click the plus to open a new tab.
speech.hint: Look at the top, just after the last tab.

steps.explain: Each tab is its own page, so your new note leaves everything else that's open alone.

speech.demonstrate: Click in the page and type a short note, like a shopping list. Press Enter at the end of each line.
speech.guide: Type your note, then press Enter.
speech.hint: Click inside the big empty area first, then type.

steps.explain: Notepad suggests your first line as the file's name when you save.

speech.demonstrate: Click File at the top left. Saving is in there.
speech.hint: Saving, opening and printing all sit in one menu.

steps.explain: The File menu holds everything about the file itself: new, open, save and print.

speech.demonstrate: Click Save as. A window opens where you choose the name and the folder.
speech.hint: You want to choose where it goes, so pick the option that asks.

steps.explain: Save as always asks for a name and a folder, so you know exactly where your note goes.

speech.demonstrate: It's going into Documents; the bar at the top says so. Type a name in File name if you like, then click Save.
speech.guide: Check the name, then click Save.
speech.hint: The button that keeps your note is at the bottom right.

steps.explain: Saved: the tab now shows the file's name, and your note is safe in Documents.

mistakes.correction: That closed the Save as window without saving. Open File, then Save as again.
